correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning after conditioning on the backward shared-reset age yields the exact mixture at finite and infinite times, and the independently marked Poisson process gives the comparator. Integration by parts verifies the same mean. Strict Poisson convexity yields strict convex order. The no-reset atomic component plus a smooth endpoint integral yields the fixed-time relative 2rt/q correction. Exact Gamma representation and a uniform-exponential-integrability normal limit for its square root yield the stationary mass including 1/sqrt(2) and exp(lambda^2/8). Stirling and conditional variance prove the claimed asymptotic and dense limit. The included diagnostic script passed, but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Current fluctuations under step initial data are a recognized physical observable. A common reset intervention preserves every one-body law and current mean, yet the count changes in strict convex order, its variance acquires an exact positive term, high-density self-averaging fails, and the leading high-count exponent changes from one at finite times to one-half at stationarity. Explicit sharp finite-time and stationary asymptotic constants separate two rare-event mechanisms and enable quantitative risk estimates.
